Set up the mail server

  1. Get the SMTP server, connection security, credentials if needed, and sender address from your mail sending service or relay administrator.

  2. Put the mail server settings in the settings file, as shown below, and apply the settings file. MMHotline connects, greets the server, checks TLS and any authentication, then quits without sending. The value “unencrypted” sends the password and alerts without encryption.

  3. Add your own email address under Contact methods. Saving the contact method sends a test message.

Settings file keys

  • SMTP server

    sending_services.mail_server.smtp_server

    The mail server's host name and port, such as smtp.example.com:587.

  • SMTP connection security

    sending_services.mail_server.smtp_connection_security

    The value “starttls” requires a successful switch to TLS on the SMTP connection. The value “implicit_tls” uses TLS from the start of the connection. The value “unencrypted” sends the password and alerts without encryption.

  • SMTP user name (optional)

    sending_services.mail_server.smtp_user_name

    For a relay that needs no authentication, leave out smtp_user_name and smtp_password.

  • SMTP password (optional)

    sending_services.mail_server.smtp_password

    Required with the SMTP user name. Spaces belong to the password.

  • Email from address

    sending_services.mail_server.email_from_address

    One plain ASCII address, such as alerts@example.com. Messages show the sender as MMHotline <email_from_address>.

Example settings

sending_services:
  mail_server:
    smtp_server: <SMTP server>
    smtp_connection_security: <SMTP connection security>
    smtp_user_name: <SMTP user name>
    smtp_password: <SMTP password>
    email_from_address: <Email from address>
Where the mail server is set up

Set in /etc/mmhotline/mmhotline_settings.yml, in sending_services.mail_server. An administrator edits the settings file with sudoedit, then runs sudo mmhotline settings apply.

Times are New York time (America/New_York), the team's time zone.
